official.deadline_note: One PSC-wide window covers all ten undergraduate PSC schemes: applications open 01 Sep 2026 and close 15 Mar 2027. No separate ministry or institutional deadline is published.
official.status_note: 'Applications for PSC Scholarships for 2027 are now open and will close on 15 March 2027.' The scheme page for PSC Scholarship states 'Applications for PSC Scholarship are now open. Application Period: 01 Sep 2026 - 15 Mar 2027.'
official.tuition_coverage_note: Cost of Degree: 'Tuition fees and other approved charges. For overseas degrees, return airfare will be provided. For mid-term candidates, tuition and other compulsory fees incurred before the award will be back paid.'
benefits: Tuition fees and other approved charges
Full salary including bonuses for those on the Uniformed Service track
Sponsorship of PSC development programmes and approved student exchange or summer programmes
Sponsorship of master's degree (if requirements are met)
Back payment of tuition and other compulsory fees for mid-term candidates
eligibility: Demonstrate Strong Leadership Qualities and Potential
Present themselves as well-rounded individuals, possessing good academic and non-academic records
Academic requirements: GCE A-levels; or International Baccalaureate; or NUS High School Diploma; or Polytechnic Diploma with merit; or other high school diploma or equivalent
Mid-term applicants: at least one semester of university results, and the application should be made before the final year of undergraduate studies
For professional schemes with a tied agency, the applicant must be undertaking an undergraduate degree in an area relevant to the tied agency
requirements: A valid Singpass account is required to access and submit the scholarship application form
The application is only considered complete when the form is submitted, the essay is completed and submitted, and all supporting documents are uploaded and submitted
A video interview link is received within 7 days of successful submission and must be completed
Applicants may apply prior to receiving final examination results; a provisional scholarship offer may be made subject to confirmation upon release of final results
With effect from 21 December 2023 the application portal is not supported on mobile devices and tablets; a laptop or desktop computer is required
documents: Secondary 4 / Year 4 Year End School Academic Reports (including results and teachers' comments)
Secondary 4 / Year 4 Co-curricular Activities (CCA) and Community Involvement Programme (CIP) Records

Certificates of Academic Qualification Obtained (e.g. GCE O-level, GCE A-level, International Baccalaureate Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, Polytechnic Diploma, other high school diploma or equivalent)

Mid-term applicants additionally: University Academic Transcripts; University CCA Records; Employment Testimonials (if applicable); NS Certificate of Service and Testimonial (if applicable); Public Service Internship Testimonials (if applicable)
selection_criteria: Psychometric Assessments, meant to assess general, verbal and numerical reasoning abilities
Game-Based Assessments, which provide an understanding of the candidate's natural attributes
Psychological Interview, providing an in-depth report of motivations, interests and values, to give the board a sense of who the candidate is
Panel interview with the Public Service Commission (PSC) Scholarships Selection Board (PSSB); only candidates who complete all assessments will undergo this
Performance across the assessments is taken into consideration when deciding on further shortlisting
coverage: Cost of Degree: tuition fees and other approved charges; return airfare for overseas degrees; tuition and other compulsory fees incurred before the award are back paid for mid-term candidates
Allowances: maintenance and other allowances, paid only from the point of award for mid-term candidates; full salary including bonuses on the Uniformed Service track
Development Programmes: sponsorship of PSC development programmes and approved student exchange or summer programmes, with facilitated internship opportunities
Master's Programme (if applicable): sponsorship of master's degree, if requirements are met
application_method: Prepare the supporting documents first, for ease of uploading and cross-checking
Complete the application form sections: Personal & Family Details, Education History, Achievements, Career and Course Preferences, University Applications, Other Details, Declaration
Submit the essay, upload all supporting documents, then submit the application
Receive the video interview link within 7 days and complete the video interview
If shortlisted, attend psychometric assessments, game-based assessments and a psychological interview, then the PSSB panel interview
official.application_route: Apply online through the PSC scholarship portal using a Singpass login on a laptop or desktop, submit the form with the essay and supporting documents, then complete the video interview sent within 7 days.
official.international_eligibility: Not eligible. Applicants must be Singapore Citizens, so international students cannot apply.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: PSC Scholarship holders may study at local or overseas universities and choose from a diverse range of courses relevant to the Public Service, subject to the PSC's approval. The ten schemes are grouped as Open, Engineering, Foreign Service, Judicial Service/Legal Service, Medicine/Dentistry, Public Finance, Sustainability, Teaching Service and Uniformed Service (SAF Scholarship, SPF Scholarship); professional schemes with a tied agency require a degree relevant to that agency.
official.duration: Maximum duration of undergraduate study by country of study: UK 3 years, US 4 years, Others 2 years; additional year(s) granted for a master's are 1 year in SG, 1 year in the UK, 2 years in the US and 2 years in other countries. For PSC Scholarship (Medicine/Dentistry), study is in Singapore only: up to 5 years for medicine and up to 4 years for dentistry. For mid-term applicants the duration of study includes the duration completed before the award.
official.description: The PSC Scholarship is the premier government scholarship awarded based on merit, offering varied career pathways in the Singapore Public Service through three main career paths: Public Administration, Professional Service and Uniformed Service. Scholarship holders are described as a diverse group of outstanding young talents who are all-rounded and committed to serving Singapore and Singaporeans.
official.program_type: Government undergraduate scholarship for the Singapore Public Service, across three career tracks (Public Administration, Professional Service, Uniformed Service)

verification.notes: PSC publishes the value of award only as coverage categories (tuition and other approved charges, maintenance and other allowances, return airfare for overseas degrees, development programmes, master's sponsorship) with no monetary figure, so amount, currency and period are null. No English-language test or MOI requirement and no research-proposal requirement are published anywhere on the PSC scholarship pages; the 'English Speaking Countries' label in PSC's tables is a bond-length category, not a language requirement. Official pages checked were last updated 1 September 2026 (scholarship overview), 13 August 2026 (undergraduate listing) and 20 August 2026 (application process).

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a Public Service career programme with a scholarship attached, not as a study grant: you apply in September, sit psychometric and game-based assessments plus a psychological interview, and only then face the PSC Scholarships Selection Board, with final outcomes arriving as late as June. The money is defined by coverage rather than a cash figure - tuition and approved charges, maintenance allowances, and return airfare for overseas degrees - so there is no published stipend number to budget against, and you should plan your own gap. The bond is the real cost: four years if you study in Singapore, five for a non-English-speaking country and six for an English-speaking country, with Medicine/Dentistry running to six years. Applying before your final examination results is allowed and can produce a provisional offer, but that offer only crystallises once the results are released.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizen school leavers, or current undergraduates up to their penultimate year, with strong all-round academic and co-curricular records who genuinely want a Public Service career and can accept a four to six year bond.
application_readiness_checklist: Register and test your Singpass login weeks before 15 March, and submit from a laptop or desktop browser since the portal explicitly does not support phones or tablets
Assemble Secondary 4 year-end reports with teacher comments, Secondary 4 and pre-tertiary CCA and CIP records, and certificates for every qualification in one folder before opening the form
Mid-term applicants: add university transcripts, university CCA records, employment testimonials, NS Certificate of Service and any Public Service Internship testimonial
Write the essay in a separate document first, then keep a clear evening free for the video interview, which lands within seven days of submission and must be completed

Pick your target scheme early - Open, Engineering, Foreign Service, Judicial/Legal, Medicine/Dentistry, Public Finance, Sustainability, Teaching, SAF or SPF - because tied-agency schemes require a degree relevant to that agency
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the form but leaving an uploaded document unsubmitted: PSC counts an application complete only when the form, the essay and every supporting document have all been submitted
Ignoring or missing the video interview link sent within seven days
A profile that reads purely academic - PSC screens for well-roundedness, leadership and sound character, so thin CCA and CIP records hurt even with top grades
Applying to a tied-agency professional scheme with a degree unrelated to that agency
Proposing a course or university that PSC does not judge relevant to the Public Service, since course choice is subject to PSC approval
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Personal and discretionary spending beyond the maintenance allowance, plus anything PSC does not classify as an approved charge; because no allowance figure is published on the official pages, you cannot budget the stipend from the source alone and should model your own cost of living.
document_audit: Secondary 4 / Year 4 reports must include teachers' comments, not just results - a plain result slip is not what PSC asks for
Preliminary examination results are explicitly not required, so do not pad the file with them or substitute them for final certificates
Every qualification certificate named on the page (O-level, A-level, IB, NUS High School Diploma, Polytechnic Diploma or equivalent) must be uploaded, not merely keyed into the form
Mid-term files routinely miss the NS Certificate of Service and Public Service Internship testimonial - both are listed where applicable
alerts: The cycle is long: assessments and interviews run from August through to June of the following year, so hold your university options open and expect to wait
Interview outcomes include 'Not suitable for PSC Scholarship' and 'Referred to Ministries' - a referral is not an offer, and the ministry may simply go silent
For mid-term awards, tuition and compulsory fees are back paid but allowances only start from the point of award, so the first semester is effectively self-funded
'English Speaking Countries' in PSC's bond table is a bond-length band of six years, not an English proficiency requirement - do not assume an IELTS or TOEFL score is needed
Medicine and Dentistry scholarships require study in Singapore only, for up to five years (medicine) or four years (dentistry)
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Singpass login on a desktop browser, then form plus essay plus document upload; a video interview link arrives within seven days; shortlisted candidates run assessments and a PSSB panel interview before an outcome by June.
